text:
Priya Shah: Hey team — quick question. We're piloting an on-call coverage pool for mid-sprint PTO so engineers can 'latch' their day into the pool instead of doing a 1:1 swap. What approvals do we need from People Ops + eng? Any concerns about using an approval bot to auto-assign coverage and update rotation?

Jon Reyes: Sounds useful. For eng we'd need manager signoff + oncall lead ack. Also need a visible UI/record of who's in the pool. +1 to automation if there's a manual fallback.

Marta Lopez: From People Ops perspective: manager approval is required for PTO that overlaps any release blackout windows, otherwise manager can delegate approval. For tracking we need start/end dates, replacement/backup, and whether the time is paid or unpaid. The bot is fine but it must write an audit entry (for payroll & compliance).

Priya Shah: Good notes. Could the bot also create a short ticket in the rotation board? Example idea for the flow: `@people-ops-bot request-pto --date 2026-04-15 --oncall-latch=true --backup=@alice` so ops gets a ticket + slack approval.

Jon Reyes: If `--oncall-latch=true` the bot should rebalance the rotation and ping the oncall lead. Small concern: rotation rebalance during release days might be risky — we should allow an override flag and require manager confirm for critical weeks.

Elena Park: I approve this approach for my org as long as I get a notification and one-click approve. Also would like an opt-out toggle per sprint for weeks where we freeze changes.

people-ops-bot: Auto-check: requested date `2026-04-15` is not in global blackout windows ✅ Manager approval required: yes. Suggested next step: notify manager (Elena Park) and oncall lead (Jon Reyes). Reply `approve` or `deny`, or `approve --notify-oncall=false`.

Marta Lopez: We'll require the bot to persist an audit record with: employee, manager, request ts, approval ts, backup person, payroll bucket. Please include a human-readable reason field so we can triage anomalies.

Priya Shah: Where should we document the new flow? I propose: 1) short runbook in Confluence under "On-call coverage pool", 2) one-line addition to the PTO policy about latching and pools, and 3) a sample demo video.

Jon Reyes: Agree. Also add a metric to watch: `time_to_backfill` and `manual_swaps_per_week` so we can detect if the pool increases churn.

Marta Lopez: I'll draft the runbook and the minimal policy blurb. Here's a tiny example payload the bot can emit for approvals:

```
{
  "employee": "priya.shah",
  "date": "2026-04-15",
  "latch": true,
  "backup": "alice.m",
  "manager": "elena.park",
  "approval": "pending",
  "audit_id": "ao-2167894321-1"
}
```

Marta Lopez: We should also add a payroll bucket field so payroll doesn't accidentally mark pool days as unpaid swaps.

Priya Shah: Great — I'll build a quick prototype of the Slack command + ticket creation and demo on Friday. Thanks everyone! :rocket: 

Jon Reyes: Thanks — ping us when the prototype is ready, we'll test on our team. :thumbsup:

people-ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: prototype demo on Friday 10:00am. Calendar invite sent to participants.
